title: Audit: crypto2dev-shim 2026-04-21 (pass 3)
description: Third-pass audit of crypto2dev_port.c after wolfssl-yjw and wolfssl-qsi fixes. Checks encrypt/decrypt parity, devCtx lifecycle, FIPS minimums, wire protocol safety, return code semantics, streaming state, pool/global state, and observability.
notes:
Confidence calibration — updated after ASAN run and code review of wc_AesSetKey.

AES key minimum gap: CLOSED. wc_AesSetKey (wolfcrypt/src/aes.c:4216) enforces keylen == 16 || 24 || 32 before returning. Any caller supplying a non-standard key length gets BAD_FUNC_ARG from wc_AesSetKey, not from the shim. The shim stores whatever keySz it receives, but wc_AesSetKey fails and the Aes object is never used in a well-behaved caller. Not a shim defect.

ASAN run (2026-04-21): PASS — 0 errors.
Build: ./configure --enable-crypto2dev --enable-crypto2devsim --enable-crypto2devtest --enable-cryptocb --enable-cryptocbutils=copy,free,setkey --enable-debug --disable-shared CFLAGS='-g -O1 -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer' LDFLAGS='-fsanitize=address'
Checks: detect_leaks=1, halt_on_error=1, check_initialization_order=1, detect_stack_use_after_return=1
23 crypto2dev sub-tests passed: SHA-256 KAT, AES-CBC KAT, HMAC-SHA256 KAT (single+two-chunk), HMAC short-key fallback, HMAC oversized rejection, HMAC lifecycle, GCM empty-plaintext, GCM oversized-AAD rejection, GCM truncated-tag, GCM sub-minimum tag, GCM oversized-tag, ECDSA P-256 round-trip, AES COPY devCtx guard, HMAC COPY devCtx guard, TLS 1.3 devId routing (SHA-256 SW fallback, HMAC HW, AES-GCM HW), TLS 1.2 integration (assign_devid, AES-CBC, HMAC-SHA256).

Revised confidence:
  Encrypt/decrypt parity: 98% — ASAN confirms no memory errors on both paths.
  devCtx lifecycle: 97% — ASAN with detect_leaks and stack-use-after-return confirms no leaks or dangling accesses on normal paths. One future-proof gap (ECC COPY, 681.4) remains.
  FIPS minimums: 98% — AES key minimum confirmed enforced by wolfSSL software path.
  Wire protocol: 100% — all zeroing/length-check patterns confirmed; ASAN no uninitialized-read errors.
  Streaming state: 100% — CBC IV, CTR counter, HMAC accumulation buffer all exercised by KATs under ASAN.
  Remaining gaps: error injection paths (pool exhaustion, INIT ioctl failure during Final) not covered by existing KATs. These would require fault injection to exercise.
